nodes.description: Cardiomyocytes isolated from heterozygous Erma mice have irregular spontaneous Ca2+ transients, and siRNA knockdown of ERMA in human iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes abolishes their Mg2+ oscillations and disturbs Ca2+ cycling. Cytosolic Mg2+ modulates cardiac Ca2+ handling, which is the proposed link. Ca2+ cycling has not been studied in patient-derived cardiomyocytes.

nodes.description: ERMA pumps Mg2+ from the cytosol into the ER lumen, which is a major store of free intracellular Mg2+. Knockdown in HepG2 cells and knockout in mouse embryonic fibroblasts lower resting ER Mg2+, and the uptake defect is independent of SERCA and of ER Ca2+ handling. ERMA binds TUSC3, the product of another recessive intellectual disability gene, in an ER Mg2+ transport complex. The earliest reports described TMEM94 as a nuclear membrane protein; subcellular fractionation places it with SERCA2 in the ER. All measurements are from cell lines, mouse embryonic fibroblasts and primary hepatocytes; ER Mg2+ has not been measured in patient cells.

nodes.description: Biallelic frameshift, nonsense and splice-site variants truncate TMEM94 (ERMA) and reduce its expression in patient cells. ERMA is an endoplasmic reticulum P-type ATPase with actuator, nucleotide-binding and phosphorylation domains and a C-terminal GMN motif. When patient alleles (W266Pfs30, R265Sfs7, A300Q328del, R922stop) are expressed in cells, they lose ATP-dependent Mg2+ uptake almost completely.
